title: Complements to Li’s Criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
version: author-hosted 12-page manuscript; version date not verified
read_scope: Only manuscript pp.3–5: Theorem 1, its proof and Corollary 1 inspected as rendered pages. Not a whole-paper substantive reading or audit. Local text extraction is encoded/unreadable.
main_result: Theorem 1 (manuscript p.3) for a multiset R with 1 not in R and sum_rho (1+|Re rho|)/(1+|rho|)^2 finite: Re rho<=1/2 for every rho iff sum_rho Re[1-(1-1/rho)^(-n)]>=0 for every positive integer n; equivalently these real sums have subexponential lower bounds for every epsilon>0. Corollary 1 (pp.4–5), adding reflection and conjugation symmetry and excluding0,1, gives the familiar positive-power Li criterion for the critical line.
proof_architecture: Off-half-plane extremal moduli attained finitely under summability
Separate maximal-modulus roots from strictly smaller remainder
Simultaneous Diophantine approximation makes extremal phase cosines approach their common maximum
Reflection and conjugation convert half-plane to critical-line criterion and inverse powers to positive powers
limitations: Every-n quantifier essential; no finite-prefix implication is stated.
Not a source-specific arithmetic theorem alone: the main criterion applies to general multisets.
Arithmetic explicit-formula sections were not read in this independent track.
research_questions: Which additional arithmetic structure could supply uniform tail control for finite Li-positivity certificates?
Can finite-data robustness bounds be quantified in classes satisfying stronger growth and explicit-formula constraints?
reusable_lemma: The inverse-power root formula is natural for derivatives at s=1; reflection symmetry is required before using the standard positive-power zero sum.
